analysis.title: Too Rich To Save, Too Backstopped To Short: Hartnett Stays Risk-Off As King Dollar Becomes A 'Wrecking Ball'
key_insights: Hartnett remains tactically risk-off. The mid-November condition for a year-end rally failed because payrolls and CPI came in hot. He now says the global tightening cycle ends at the April FOMC at the earliest and cut his oil trigger to WTI $70 from $80.
He added the dollar as a third item on his risk-off checklist, alongside oil and yields. All three moved the wrong way last week. He expects the dollar to peak in February or March.
Weekly scoreboard YTD: oil 54.0%, US stocks 10.9%, global stocks 8.8%, US dollar 4.9%, cash 3.2%, HY -0.5%, IG -2.8%, govt bonds -3.6%, gold -10.4%, bitcoin -18.9%. Bitcoin trails gold by 8.5 points.

Why save: US household equity wealth is down about $3tn over the past month but up about $9tn in 2026 and $19tn since Jan 2025, on a $74tn base. Consumption is 70% of GDP and the wealthy feel flush, which makes a recession hard to get. BofA private clients' equity allocation fell to 65.2%, a seven-month low.

Why short: Taiwan announced a $15bn stabilization fund, Korea suspended its margin rule that forces liquidation of leveraged retail positions, and China's national team keeps buying. Hartnett says global policymakers treat stock markets as too big to fail, which is why no one is short.

Positioning: record year of inflows to global equities. Many investors feel bearish but few are short or underweight. Stock funds took in $98.3bn in the week, the most since June. Goldman's Prime desk sees hedge funds shorting single-name AI stocks, with US tech long/short at 1.5, the lowest since 2016, while covering 8.6% of ETF shorts.
BofA Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 7.4 from 7.2, neutral territory. Hedge fund positioning is at the 60th percentile, equity flows at the 96th and fund manager positioning at the 100th.

Why risk-off: Hartnett counts more than 70 central bank hikes from Jun 2026 to May 2027. Cyclicals are rolling over (lumber -21%, metals -11%, 'blue-collar' semis -26%), and he expects the next revision to boom forecasts (5-6% nominal GDP, over 15% EPS in 2027) to be down.

His stance ends when rate hikes end and financial conditions ease through WTI below $70, the 10Y Treasury below 4.5% (likely Dec-Jan) and a lower dollar (peak Feb-Mar). At Friday's close none was met. WTI was about $89, the 10Y 5.15% and the DXY 103.42.

S&P scenarios: above 8,000 is the bull case (dip-buying flows, equal-weight S&P back to highs, JNK/SPX/XBD/TSM above their 200-day averages, Trump-Xi-Putin APEC meeting confirming peak oil). Below 7,000 is the bear case (dollar spike, liquidity shortage, central banks hiking into a slowdown). The S&P closed at 7,562.

The article contrasts consensus S&P earnings growth of 18% in Hartnett's chart with Goldman's 11% for 2027. Its napkin math puts forward EPS near $364 and the index near 7,100 at the same multiple, about 6% below the consensus-based level. Goldman keeps an 8,700 target.

Hartnett's best 2026 pair trades: long oil/short crypto, long energy/short discretionary, long semis/short telecom, long small cap value/short mega cap growth, long Taiwan/short China, long cyber/short defense. The S&P is on track for a fourth straight double-digit year, which has happened only three times since 1871.

Politics: 8 Senate seats flipped GOP to DEM. Hartnett says this reinforces his 'Anything But Bonds' allocation and lowers the bar for fiscal stimulus. He says investors won't touch Treasuries until they yield 5.5-6.5%. The 30Y closed at 5.48% and the 20Y at 5.53%. The article notes this conflicts with needing the 10Y at 4.5% to turn bullish.

Flows (EPFR, week through Wednesday): stocks +$98.3bn, bonds +$0.3bn, gold +$49mn, crypto -$1.9bn, cash -$17.9bn. Treasuries had $0.6bn of outflows, the first since June. EM debt lost $1.5bn. China equity funds are on a record five-week streak of $88.0bn.

Goldman's FX team sees one more leg of dollar strength (EUR/USD 1.08 in three months) before a turn to 1.15 by end-2027. The trade-weighted dollar is about 13% overvalued. The article says this timing matches Hartnett's dollar peak call.
Upcoming events: Nov 17 BofA Global FMS and Nvidia's first earnings without Jensen Huang. Nov 18 APEC summit in Shenzhen and Anthropic IPO pricing. FOMC hikes priced for Dec 9, Jan 27 and Mar 17.

The article's own view agrees with Hartnett on direction but doubts the route. It sides with the bond market and argues a backstopped market 'has to fail a little' first. It notes foreigners sold $48bn of Taiwanese stocks in a month against Taiwan's $15bn fund.

risk_factors: Dollar spike and global liquidity shortage.
Central banks hiking into a slowdown, with more than 70 hikes expected from Jun 2026 to May 2027.
Higher credit spreads and lower stocks ending the inflationary K-shaped boom and AI capex cycle.
10Y yield at 5.15% after weak foreign demand at auction (lowest since October 2023), with all three coupon auctions tailing.
Oil depends on the US-Iran outcome.
Consensus earnings growth of 18% may be too high versus Goldman's 11%.
Treasury reported the worst October deficit on record.
charts_described: Weekly Hartnett scoreboards over the last seven weeks, where the dollar is the only line ending at its high.
Chart of the ratio of large growth to small value, which peaked in November 2025 at almost exactly its March 2000 high and has been falling since.
BofA Bull & Bear Indicator chart with hedge fund positioning at the 60th percentile, equity flows at the 96th and fund manager positioning at the 100th.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's Prime desk saw hedge funds sell US stocks for a fifth week in six, mostly through fresh single-name shorts. US tech long/short fell to 1.5, the lowest since 2016.
The prior week had the biggest hedge fund degross since Covid, which took net leverage to a five-year low. The same funds covered 8.6% of ETF shorts, the most in seven months.
BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.4 (the 'old' indicator is 6.4). Fund manager positioning is at the 100th percentile, equity flows at the 96th and hedge funds at the 60th.

The Nasdaq had its worst day since Covid nine days earlier. Hartnett watches the Nov 17 FMS: boom expectations were 47% in October with cash at 3.9%. Cash above 4.2% with a drop in boom expectations would mean sentiment is less of a headwind. Cash below 3.7% means not enough fear to buy.
geopolitical: Trump said 'we don't need a deal' with Iran, which lifted WTI back to about $89 after Brent briefly broke below $90.
Trump, Xi and Putin are expected at the Nov 18 APEC summit in Shenzhen. Hartnett sees it as a possible confirmation of peak oil.
Taiwan, Korea and China took stabilization measures after the post-midterm crash in Asia.
Eight Senate seats flipped from GOP to DEM in the midterms.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's FX team sees dollar strength before a turn, matching Hartnett's dollar peak in February or March.
Goldman's Oppenheimer sees 2027 S&P EPS growth of 11% against 18% in Hartnett's chart of consensus.
Goldman still has an 8,700 S&P target.
Goldman economists added a March hike on Wednesday and a third hike overall.
Goldman says AI capex is close to peaking.

tension_points.bull_case: Above 8,000 if buy-the-dip flows persist, the equal-weight S&P returns to highs, JNK, SPX, XBD and TSM hold above their 200-day averages, and the Nov 18 APEC meeting confirms peak oil. Households hold $19tn of gains, and policymakers have backstopped stocks.
tension_points.bear_case: Below 7,000 on a dollar spike, liquidity shortage and central banks hiking into a slowdown. Goldman's 11% earnings growth versus 18% consensus implies about 7,100 at the same multiple.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bull case needs SPX above 8,000 with JNK, SPX, XBD and TSM at or above their 200-day averages. Bear case triggers below 7,000.

tension_points.bull_case: Hartnett expects the 10Y below 4.5% in Dec-Jan, WTI below $70 (called underway) and a dollar peak in Feb-Mar, which would turn him constructive.
tension_points.bear_case: The checklist went zero for three. The 10Y is 5.15%, WTI about $89 and the DXY at a 2026 high. Hartnett also says buyers avoid Treasuries until 5.5-6.5%, which the article calls an unresolved tension.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 10Y below 4.5%, WTI below $70 and a falling dollar would end the risk-off stance. A November FMS with boom expectations high and cash below 3.7% means not enough fear to buy.

tension_points.bull_case: Taiwan, Korea and China intervened and the Taiex rebounded about 14% off its low, so nobody wants to be short.
tension_points.bear_case: Foreigners sold $48bn of Taiwanese stocks in a month against a $15bn fund. The article says a market too big to fail usually has to fail a little first.
